what: A short text appears on the screen. You read it out loud after a short time to prepare.
tests: Reading and speaking: saying every word clearly, with natural speed and phrasing.

scoring.note: Pearson's page lists these scored traits.

strategy: Use the preparation time to read the text silently and find the phrase breaks (commas, full stops, 'and', 'but').
Find difficult words and say them quietly in your head.
Start speaking just after the tone. Do not wait a long time: the microphone can stop after a few seconds of silence.
Read in phrases of three to six words at a steady speed. Stress the important words.
If you make a mistake, keep going. Do not go back and repeat.
example_prompt: Many towns now collect food waste separately. The waste is turned into compost for parks and farms, which reduces the amount sent to landfill.

strong.answer: Reads every word, pauses at the commas and full stop, keeps a smooth pace and stresses 'food waste', 'compost' and 'landfill'.
strong.why: All words are there, the phrasing sounds natural and the stressed words help the meaning.

medium.answer: Reads every word but stops before 'compost' and 'landfill' and says them slowly, one sound at a time.
medium.why: Content is complete, but the stops break the flow and make the speech sound uneven.

weak.answer: Misses 'separately', goes back to repeat 'turned into', and has a long silence in the middle.
weak.why: Missing words lower content; going back and long silences lower fluency.

mistakes: Going back to correct a word.
Reading word by word with no phrasing.
Waiting too long after the tone.
Speaking too fast to sound fluent.
